note: What a server sends to turn a unit toward something. Its identifier is wider than a byte, so it travels behind the escape. The header names the unit acting.

fields.name: kind
fields.note: What the unit's model turns to look at; not which way it faces. A client ignores 3 and above, keeping what it looked at before.

0.name: direction
0.note: x, y and z are a direction; target is not read.

1.name: point
1.note: x, y and z are a point in the world; target is not read.

2.name: unit
2.note: target is the object to look at; x, y and z are not read. Should it go, the unit looks at where it was last.

fields.name: x
fields.note: Where to look, along one ground axis, in world units.

fields.name: y
fields.note: Where to look, in height, in world units.

fields.name: z
fields.note: Where to look, along the other ground axis, in world units.

fields.name: target
fields.note: The network object being looked at, where one is named.
